customer_question: We were told similar future devices can be added to this registration for free -- is there a time limit on that, or can we keep adding derivative models indefinitely? And once a model is added, can it be sold forever?
question_variants: Will the free derivative-model addition feature expire at some point?
Does the module's spec version affect how long we can add new models for free?
If we add a model now, will we ever have to re-register it later?
actual_issue: The customer wanted to understand whether the ability to add future derivative models to the existing registration for free was available indefinitely, or whether it was tied to some expiration condition, and whether models already added would remain sellable without any future re-registration requirement.
plain_english_explanation: Adding similar future products to an existing Bluetooth registration for free isn't a feature that lasts forever on its own -- it's actually tied to how long the specific version of the Bluetooth specification that the registration's module is built on remains valid in SIG's system. Once that version is eventually retired, that particular free-addition path would no longer be available. But anything already added to the product list before that happens keeps being sellable indefinitely, regardless of what happens to that spec version afterward.
consultant_answer: As long as the registration remains valid, derivative models implementing the same module and host stack can be added to the Product List for free. The module referenced in this registration is built on Core Spec v5.0, so the product registration is also considered v5.0. The current planned deprecation date for v5.0 is 2032-02-01, so derivative models can be added to the Product List for free up until the day before that date. Models already registered to the Product List remain sellable indefinitely, unless changed by a new SIG regulation.
decision_logic: Free derivative-model addition to an existing registration is available for as long as the referenced module's underlying Core Spec version has not been deprecated by Bluetooth SIG; this is a time-bound window tied to that specific spec version's deprecation date, not an indefinite feature. Models already added to the Product List before that deprecation date remain sellable indefinitely regardless of the spec version's later status.
final_recommendation: When discussing free derivative-model addition with a customer, proactively check and communicate the deprecation date of the referenced module's underlying Core Spec version, since that date marks the deadline for adding further models for free under that registration; reassure the customer that models already added remain sellable indefinitely.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming free derivative-model addition is available indefinitely, without checking the referenced module's Core Spec version deprecation date, could cause a customer to miss the window for adding a planned future variant for free, requiring a costlier new registration instead.
